title: Submillimeter H<SUB>2</SUB>O Maser in Circinus Galaxy—a New Probe for the Circumnuclear Region of Active Galactic Nuclei
question: Is there 321 GHz H2O maser emission in the Circinus galaxy, and how does it compare with the known 22 GHz maser?

data.sensitivity: line rms ~9–11 mJy/beam per channel; continuum rms ~0.8 mJy/beam

what.value: Enclosed mass 1.7e6 Msun and Keplerian disk model for 22 GHz maser

evidence.quote: by calculation based on a Keplerian ($v$ $\propto$ $r^{-0.5}$) rotation disk model in Greenhill et al. (2003a, 2003b)

recipe.method: CASA calibration, continuum subtraction in uv, natural-weighted CLEAN cube

recipe.goal: Search for line emission and measure spectra and positions
recipe.method: Searched within 18 arcsec field over VLSR -430 to +1290 km/s; Gaussian-fitted peak positions
Keplerian v∝r^-0.5 scaling from the Greenhill disk model
assumptions: Black hole mass 1.7e6 Msun; Keplerian rotation

evidence.quote: peak flux density of which is 131 mJy beam$^{-1}$  at $V$$_{\rm LSR}$=531.1 km s$^{-1}$
The total integrated intensity estimated from all the detected H$_{2}$O$\;$emission is $\sim$14 Jy km s$^{-1}$.
The detected nuclear continuum with the total flux density of 55 mJy
it is located at a radius of $\sim$ 0.018 pc
